title: Check yourself: Where the data goes: platform, region and retention

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Linden Clinics asks a vendor to serve its patients from Europe and offers the Claude API with `inference_geo` set to `us` as the compliant option. Which assessment is right?

options.text: It meets the need, as long as the audit log itself is kept in a data store located in Europe
options.says: Ruled out because the audit log is separate from where inference runs, and "the request carries an inference geography" that the log store does not change.

options.text: It fails the need, because the pin sends the processing to the United States
options.says: The `us` pin is a United States geography, and the API has no European one.

options.text: It meets the need, since the geography of the workspace can still be set to Europe separately
options.says: Ruled out because "The workspace geography is set per workspace" and the page says it is `us` only.

options.text: It fails the need only if the clinics have not yet signed the business associate agreement in full
options.says: Ruled out because the agreement concerns health data and does not move the processing: "there is no European pin".

origin.section: Region: pin it where the platform lets you

questions.stem: Scenario: Harrow Insurance runs Claude on Amazon Bedrock and writes in its design that "zero data retention is enabled with Anthropic". What is the problem?

options.text: The statement is correct, since every platform shares one retention arrangement with the model maker
options.says: Ruled out because "Their retention, compliance and region rules are the provider's", so no arrangement is shared.

options.text: The statement holds only once a second approval has been given by the cloud provider's own sales team
options.says: Ruled out because the page gives no such approval, and says the provider's rules are "the provider's own documentation".

options.text: The arrangement belongs to the model maker, and on that platform the cloud provider does the processing
options.says: Zero data retention is an arrangement with Anthropic, and on Bedrock the cloud provider is the processor.

options.text: The statement is correct, but it must be repeated for each separate model that the company uses in production
options.says: Ruled out because the model is a separate rule ("A model that requires 30-day retention cannot satisfy a zero-retention requirement") and does not change who the processor is.
